title: Italy and Spain Agree to End Reciprocal Schengen Border Checks
detail: Italian Interior Minister Piantedosi and Spanish counterpart Grande-Marlaska agreed by phone not to extend their reciprocal border checks, restoring Schengen rules between the two countries. Italy had reintroduced checks on 1 August after the Ceuta surge; Spain responded on 8 August, and its measures were due to expire on 22 October. Meloni and Sánchez had signalled the intention to end the checks at the European Council the previous week. Both sides are to share more information. Reports differ slightly on Italy's exact start date (31 July vs 1 August).
